title: Wipeout Pure
subtitle: Anti-gravity racing arrives with the PSP
summary: Wipeout Pure is Studio Liverpool's PSP racing game, first released in North America on 24 March 2005. The FX300 league brings anti-gravity craft to a portable screen, combining high speed with airbrakes, weapons and sharply defined circuits. Set a century after Wipeout 2097, it returns to a cleaner visual direction after Wipeout Fusion. Each team offers a craft with its own balance of handling, acceleration, speed and shields. Choosing one is the beginning of learning how to carry momentum through a course without allowing the next corner to turn it into a collision.
body: Wipeout Pure is Studio Liverpool's PSP racing game, first released in North America on 24 March 2005. The FX300 league brings anti-gravity craft to a portable screen, combining high speed with airbrakes, weapons and sharply defined circuits. Set a century after Wipeout 2097, it returns to a cleaner visual direction after Wipeout Fusion. Each team offers a craft with its own balance of handling, acceleration, speed and shields. Choosing one is the beginning of learning how to carry momentum through a course without allowing the next corner to turn it into a collision.

Weapon pickups can be used against opponents or absorbed to replenish the shield, connecting attack and survival to the same resource. A player near the front may prefer to preserve a damaged craft rather than risk it for another shot. Airbrakes and careful positioning remain essential as the circuits become faster and more demanding. Knowing the route helps identify where to commit to speed and where a slight correction is worth more. The race becomes a continuing balance between the line ahead, the condition of the craft and the rivals sharing the track.

Development began in 2003 and continued through the PSP's North American launch, with new interface and production tools helping the team complete the game in time. Reviews praised its appearance, course design and overall presentation, while noting occasional performance fluctuations. Japanese and European editions followed in April and September 2005. Downloadable additions later enlarged the collection of tracks and craft. Pure became a strong demonstration of the handheld's possibilities by carrying a recognisable console series into a portable format while preserving the speed, visual discipline and musical character that defined it.

A pickup can keep the craft alive
A portable demonstration with room to grow
